title: kv: eviction throttling and heap defragmentation to stabilize KV cache memory pressure
text:
kv: eviction throttling and heap defragmentation to stabilize KV cache memory pressure

description:
Motivation: We observed intermittent OOM and large memory spikes on hosts running heavy chat workloads with long contexts. Root cause was aggressive synchronous eviction + arena fragmentation when large KV entries were repeatedly allocated/evicted in short windows. This PR introduces two complementary mitigations: 1) eviction throttling to limit concurrent synchronous evictions that can block inference threads and cause head-of-line blocking, and 2) background heap defragmentation (arena compaction) that reclaims free fragments without affecting hot-path token decode.

Design summary: Eviction throttling: add a token-aware throttler that enforces a per-GPU soft-concurrency limit for synchronous evictions. When the soft limit is reached, eviction requests are enqueued and served by a small eviction worker pool. We expose a soft_limit and burst_limit and a configurable policy (priority=age/size). Eviction work is measured in bytes evicted, not number of entries, to better reflect memory cost.

Background defragmentation: introduce defrag_worker that runs asynchronously and performs per-arena compaction during low-util windows. It coalesces small free blocks into larger contiguous free spans so future large KV items don't trigger spill/pager allocations. Compaction is incremental with tunable batch_size and a max_io_budget to avoid interfering with streaming.

Scheduler integration: scheduler now signals backpressure when async eviction queue length exceeds a threshold; this causes temporary throttling of batch sizes for new requests to avoid creating more eviction pressure. Continuous batching path was adjusted to prefer prefetched KV entries and to avoid inflating batch size when eviction backlog exists.

Implementation details: key changes in runtime/kv_cache: - allocator.rs: introduced EvictThrottler with metrics and tunables; made free/alloc paths non-blocking where possible. - eviction.rs: eviction now returns an EvictionHandle that may be executed synchronously or queued. - defrag_worker.rs: incremental compactor that walks arenas using conservative heuristics to avoid touching hot KV entries. - scheduler/slot_allocator.rs: added hook to query eviction queue length and apply temporary batch size backoff. - telemetry: new metrics kv.eviction.queue_length, kv.defrag.cycles, kv.eviction.throttled_count.

Testing and validation: unit tests cover correctness of eviction bookkeeping and handle lifecycle. Integration tests (tests/kv_cache/eviction_harness.py) reproduce fragmentation pattern from ENG-4312 and assert memory usage stabilizes under load. Perf lab runs (perf/bench_eviction.py) show reduction in 99.9th percentile memory spike and a small (1-3ms) tail latency improvement on p3-like nodes due to reduced head-of-line blocking.

Rollback plan: all new features are behind runtime.flags.kv_eviction_throttle && runtime.flags.kv_defrag_enabled. Rolling back is a config flip; merge will leave flags default-on for main but ops can disable via runtime config.

Notes: this PR intentionally avoids introducing on-disk paging by default; spill-to-disk remains opt-in for private deployments and gated behind runtime.flags.kv_spill_to_disk.


release_notes:
Reduced KV cache OOM spikes by adding eviction throttling and background defragmentation. Default behavior is non-breaking; tunables exposed under runtime.config.kv_cache.*.

review_comments:
Ethan Browne (2026-02-15): Can you clarify the decision to measure eviction budget in bytes vs entries? Concerned about pathological cases where many small entries overwhelm queue. Response: We measure bytes to reflect real memory cost; added per-entry cost cap and a per-item weight so pathological many-small-entries are gated.
Lia Chen (2026-02-16): Defrag touching arenas worries me for latency sensitive tails. Did you add heuristics to avoid hot entries? Response: Yes — defrag skips arenas with recent access hotness above threshold and uses max_io_budget per cycle. We also added an opt-out flag for single-tenant machines.
Samir Gupta (2026-02-17): Integration tests flaky on aarch64 CI run. Request: add a short jitter to eviction worker to avoid contention. Response: Added randomized backoff and increased test timeouts. Re-ran CI.
Ethan Browne (2026-02-18): LGTM after tests pass. Approved.

perf_summary:
Lab perf: baseline spike scenario (long chat workloads) showed peak RSS spikes of ~9.6GB -> after patch steady peaks ~7.2GB (25% reduction). 99th token latency reduced 1.8ms on average; 99.9th latency reduced 4.6ms. Eviction-related IO/CPU overhead below 2% in steady-state. Memory fragmentation measured at arena-level reduced from estimated 18% lost bytes to ~5% on synthetic churn workload.
